defect_class: A status transition checks the current state in a read, then writes the new state with an update not conditioned on that state, so concurrent transitions both pass the check and the last writer wins.
why_picked: 1. Defect class: a persisted state transition guards its source state in a read and then writes unconditionally, so two concurrent transitions from the same state both succeed. 2. The robustness principle covers emit/accept strictness, fail-fast and graceful degradation but names no rule for concurrent state changes, check-then-act or conditional writes; a grep for race, concurrent and compare-and-set across engineering-principles.md, implement.md and sdd-dispatch.md finds nothing that applies. 3. It generalises to every persisted state machine a backend writes — review, publish, invite accept, order or payment status — in any language. 4. It states a principle (put the source-state guard in the write itself), not a special case of this task.
before:
Be strict about what you emit and defensive about what you accept, fail fast on
programmer error, degrade gracefully on environmental error, and make every failure
observable.
after:
Be strict about what you emit and defensive about what you accept, fail fast on
programmer error, degrade gracefully on environmental error, and make every failure
observable.
A state transition on shared persisted data puts its source-state check in the write
itself — a conditional update (`where state = <expected>`) or compare-and-set whose
zero-row result is a conflict — never a read followed by an unconditional write.
